name: ontosage:AccessEvent
description: An aggregate-queryable entry event at an entrance. Per-person queries are denied by inference-class policy.

name: ontosage:AccessibilityFeature
description: A feature provided for accessibility: hearing loop, tactile paving, Changing Places facility, accessible WC, power-assisted door, accessible parking bay. An Amenity subclass so the existing capability resolver locates it with no new code.

name: ontosage:AccessibleRoute
description: A SURVEYED journey between an arrival point and a destination, carrying the facts a disabled visitor actually asks for: entrance, step-free or not, seated rests, how the doors operate, which lift and whether it is in service, how much time to allow, how busy it is, and a non-telephone assistance contact. surveyedOn and surveyedBy are required because every question this answers uses the word 'verified' — a route inferred from geometry is a guess about somebody's journey, and a wrong guess costs them the journey. A route that is NOT step-free is published too, so it is never offered as an accessible option by omission.

name: ontosage:AccessibleToilet
description: A toilet built for wheelchair users: both a toilet facility and an accessibility feature, so a question about either finds it.

name: ontosage:AccessPermission
description: A named grant over one controlled opening to a ROLE TEMPLATE, under a time profile, with its inheritance and overrides recorded as data. NO INDIVIDUAL IS MODELLED, deliberately: identity is held at role level, so 'which entitlements does this role justify' is answerable and 'who can open this door' is not.

name: ontosage:AccessPolicy
description: A query-parameter access policy: who may see what, at which aggregation floor, resolution tier and rate. Consumed ONLY by the deterministic Policy Decision Point; cited in the evidence dossier of every answer it shapes.

name: ontosage:Alarm_Group
description: A named set of alarms handled together. Deliberately a brick:Collection and NOT a brick:Alarm: a group of alarms is not itself an alarm, and typing it as one would let it match queries asking for active alarms.

name: ontosage:AlarmEvent
description: A persisted alarm activation episode (fire panel, freezer, leak...).

name: ontosage:Amenity
description: A physical building facility or service with a human-readable location and features.

name: ontosage:AnomalyEvent
description: A persisted detector finding with a stable id: one episode per contiguous deviation (extended while it persists, closed when readings normalise).

name: ontosage:ApprovalRecord
description: Whether a subject is approved, by which ROLE, under whose authority and until when; what evidence substantiates it, referenced and dated; who is accountable and when it is next reviewed. APPROVAL AND EVIDENCE ARE SEPARATE: a subject can be approved with no evidence recorded, or evidenced but never approved, and collapsing them into one 'verified' flag would hide exactly the gap an auditor is looking for. Roles, never people.

name: ontosage:AssemblyPoint
description: Where people gather after evacuating. An Amenity subclass so 'where is the muster point' is located like any other place — but a SAFETY place, so an instance is only ever a transcription of what the building itself publishes. A position nobody published must be left unrecorded: sending people to the wrong side of a building during an evacuation is the worst answer this vocabulary could produce.

name: ontosage:AssetEngineeringProfile
description: The engineering truth about a plant item: what it was designed for, what commissioning proved, what it is observed to deliver, where it is isolated, what depends on it downstream, what it is called in every other system, how critical it is, and how long it goes unvisited. The building recorded that an AHU exists and never recorded what it was for.

name: ontosage:AssetStatus
description: The reported operational state of a lift, door, AV system, network service or amenity over an interval. An IntervalRecord because status is a thing that STARTED at a time and may still hold: 'the lift failed at 09:14 and is still out' is one record, not a flag that was overwritten.

name: ontosage:AVEquipment
description: Projector, display, lecture-capture, microphone or hybrid-conferencing rig serving a space. 94 of the supervisors' questions depend on knowing whether the teaching kit in a room works BEFORE the class starts.

name: ontosage:AVReadiness
description: One audiovisual component in a teaching room, with its state, the formats it serves, when it was last checked and the evidence reference for that check. THE AUDIO PATH IS A CHAIN: a room with a working projector, a working display and a dead microphone cannot run a lecture that needs amplification, so inAudioPath marks the links and a room's readiness for a format follows from the chain rather than from one asserted flag. No component may be recorded READY without evidence -- 'checked' without a record is a claim, and withholding a room from service on somebody's recollection is what the team is trying to avoid. The rule is conditional rather than a required column, because a component that has NEVER been tested has no check date and no reference, and that is the most important row in the register rather than one to exclude: `unevidenced` exists so it can be stated.

name: ontosage:BikeStorage
description: Cycle racks or secure bicycle storage.

name: ontosage:Booking
description: A reservation of a space for a time interval.

name: ontosage:BuildingDescription
description: The set of self-descriptive assertions carried by a brick:Building instance.

name: ontosage:Cafe
description: A café, canteen, or catering outlet.

name: ontosage:Capability
description: Anything a stakeholder can ask a building about via OntoSage.

name: ontosage:CirculationTime
description: How long it takes to get from one part of the building to another, by the walking route and by the step-free route separately. Floor-to-floor rather than room-to-room, because a room-pair matrix grows as the square of the room count and the floor change is what dominates the time.

name: ontosage:CleaningTask
description: One unit of cleaning work: a zone, an area within it, the standard that applies, how often it recurs, the shift that owns it and the time the area must be ready. Status is READ from the register, never inferred from dates: a caretaker sent to a suspended area wastes a shift, and a suspended area silently omitted is worse.

name: ontosage:ClosurePeriod
description: An interval during which a space, floor or the whole building is closed or restricted. Opening hours say what is NORMAL; a closure says what overrides it, and 271 of the supervisors' questions depend on the override being visible.

name: ontosage:CompetencyRecord
description: A training, induction or authorisation requirement attached to a ROLE and an area or task — deliberately never to a person. The answerable form is: this area requires these competencies. No building TTL carries personal training records.

name: ontosage:Complaint
description: A dissatisfaction report (noise, cleanliness, temperature, service).

name: ontosage:ComplianceCheck
description: A dated statutory or policy check (fire alarm test, legionella flush, LOLER, PAT...). Due/overdue is computed from dueDate vs completedDate.

name: ontosage:ConditionSurvey
description: A dated inspection recording an asset condition grade and remaining life. Brick models what an asset IS and where it sits; it has no vocabulary for how worn it is, which is the clearest case for extending OCBV rather than forcing Brick to carry it.

name: ontosage:ConfigurationPeriod
description: An interval during which a point's location, calibration and configuration were stable. Readings are interpreted against the period covering their timestamp, so a window spanning a boundary can be flagged rather than silently averaged across a discontinuity.

name: ontosage:ContinuityProvision
description: One service, the space or system it normally depends on, and what happens when that is unavailable: the alternative location, the path to it, the capacity that alternative can carry, how long the service can run before the alternative is needed, and when the arrangement was last proved. recordStatus is the owner's recorded state; an alternative with no proving evidence is recorded as unverified rather than as a provision, because a continuity answer that offers an untested option is worse than one that says there is none.

name: ontosage:Contract
description: A service, maintenance or supply agreement with a provider, over a term, covering a named scope. Distinct from Warranty: a contract is bought, a warranty accompanies an asset — they have different owners and routinely disagree, which should be REPORTED rather than resolved.

name: ontosage:CoordinationFunction
description: One coordination function for one operational period: its accountable role, primary system and that system's state, the approved fallback, the activation criterion and whether that criterion is evidenced as met. UNKNOWN IS A FIRST-CLASS STATE. In an incident, 'we have not established whether this is met' and 'this is not met' lead to different decisions, and a register collapsing them into one empty cell would be actively dangerous -- so criterionState carries an explicit unknown, and a row without an evidence reference cannot be recorded as met. The approved fallback sits beside the function it replaces, because a fallback that must be looked up elsewhere during an incident is not a fallback.

name: ontosage:CostLine
description: One line of the building's ledger, carrying budget, actual, committed and accrued as SEPARATE amounts. Free balance is budget minus all three, and a register that folded commitments into actuals could report money as available when a purchase order has already claimed it -- 'decision-ready free balance' is precisely the figure after all three. varianceCause is recorded rather than inferred, because a line can move on price, quantity, timing or scope and the number alone cannot say which, while the remedies differ.

name: ontosage:Database
description: A registered time-series backend holding sensor readings; the object of ref:storedAt, resolved to a connection through database_registry.yaml.

name: ontosage:Department
description: An organisational function that operates, maintains, secures or administers the building, with its scope, coverage hours, agreed response target, request channel and escalation route recorded as data. Names functions and contact routes only — never individuals.

name: ontosage:DisclosureRule
description: A rule saying which fields of a view of the building may be shown as they stand, which must be suppressed or aggregated before sharing, which need a caveat and which must be confirmed by their owner first. Declared so that a question about those rules is recognised as one about a register the building may not hold, and is answered by naming what is and is not recorded — instead of by describing a different view of the building that happens to share the words 'space' and 'fields'.

name: ontosage:DoorHardware
description: One controlled opening — door, shutter, barrier or turnstile — and how it behaves when power or the fire alarm changes state: its fail state on power loss, any hold-open device, how it is released, and which system commands it. recordStatus is the owner's recorded state; failStateOnPowerLoss is recorded per opening because a fire shutter and an escape door on one circuit fail in opposite directions by design.

name: ontosage:DrinkingWater
description: Drinking fountain, water cooler or bottle-filling point.

name: ontosage:Emergency_Generator
description: Standby generation plant serving life-safety and critical loads during a supply failure. Brick 1.4 defines Emergency_Generator_Alarm and _Status points but no equipment class to hang them on.

name: ontosage:EvacuationProvision
description: A named arrangement for getting a person out of the building who cannot simply walk down the stairs: a refuge point, an evacuation chair, a communication unit, or a personal emergency evacuation plan held at role level. Deliberately does NOT record who any plan belongs to — the plan's EXISTENCE, location and review date are operational facts anyone may need; its subject is not.

name: ontosage:EventActivity
description: One item inside a PublicEvent's agenda: its position, start, duration, location, whether a companion may attend and whether it is optional. An agenda is not a property of an event -- it is a sequence of things with their own durations and rules, which is why it is rows. companionPolicy is per ACTIVITY because a campus tour and a one-to-one admissions conversation can sit inside the same open day and differ, and a family planning their day needs it at that level or the answer is wrong for half the visit. isOptional exists so 'we only have two hours, what should we prioritise' is answerable by dropping what the events office marked optional rather than by inventing a preference.

name: ontosage:Facility
description: A named lab, workshop, or teaching space (makerspace, trading room, cyber lab).

name: ontosage:FaultReport
description: A reported equipment/facility fault (leak, broken light, broken lift). Typically ties to a Module A ontosage:MaintenanceIssue and, via ontosage:aboutEquipment, to the brick:Equipment.

name: ontosage:Feedback
description: General feedback about the building or OntoSage itself.

name: ontosage:FireSafetyAsset
description: A physical fire precaution — detection, alarm, suppression, a fire door, a compartment penetration or an escape provision — with the date it was last tested, the evidence for that test, the standard it is held to and the defects open against it. Recorded separately from general plant because a fire precaution that is merely PRESENT proves nothing: the question is always when it was last proved to work.

name: ontosage:FirstAidPoint
description: First-aid point or defibrillator (AED). Where the building models AED devices as equipment, the amenity should name their locations so the question is answered from the building's own graph.

name: ontosage:ForecastSkill
description: Measured predictive skill for one (modality x horizon) on THIS building, from walk-forward backtesting. Cited in every forecast answer; makes 'how good are your forecasts?' SPARQL-answerable.

name: ontosage:HandoverRecord
description: A project handover, as-built revision, commissioning certificate or O and M manual, linked to the assets it describes. This is what a claim of commissioned must REST on: the five-part verification gate reads it, so a commissioning state with no handover record behind it is unverified by construction.

name: ontosage:HazardControl
description: A recognised hazard present in the building, the control applied to it, the regime that tests the control and when that test is next due. One class serves COSHH substances, local exhaust ventilation, asbestos-containing materials and water hygiene because they share exactly this shape — a hazard that is managed rather than removed, whose safety depends on a test somebody has to keep doing. Modelling them separately would have produced four near-identical registers and four places for the same question to be half-answered.

name: ontosage:Heat_Pump
description: Reversible heat-transfer plant. Brick 1.4 defines only the compound condensing-unit variants (Heat_Pump_Condensing_Unit and its air/ground-source subclasses), none of which fit a whole-unit instance.

name: ontosage:IncidentRecord
description: Something that went wrong or nearly did: injury, near miss, property damage, security breach or environmental release, with what was done immediately, what the investigation concluded, whether it is externally reportable and what remains outstanding. A near miss is recorded in the SAME register as an injury deliberately — separating them is how an organisation stops seeing that the two have the same cause.

name: ontosage:InformationTopic
description: A factual/policy topic: opening hours, contacts, WiFi, GDPR, accessibility, transport.

name: ontosage:IntervalRecord
description: Abstract supertype for anything that happens over a time interval with a lifecycle: bookings, work orders, access events, alarms, compliance checks, anomaly episodes. Never instantiated directly.

name: ontosage:Kitchenette
description: Shared microwave, kettle and fridge for occupants' own food and drink.

name: ontosage:KnowledgeTopic
description: An informational, procedural, or maintenance topic a stakeholder can ask about.

name: ontosage:Lift
description: A passenger lift; useful for accessibility questions.

name: ontosage:Lighting_Command
description: A writable point controlling luminaire state or level.

name: ontosage:Locker
description: Storage lockers for occupants/students.

name: ontosage:MaintenanceIssue
description: A fault type and who to report it to: leak, broken light, broken lift, heating fault. MAY reference the brick:Equipment it concerns via ontosage:aboutEquipment.

name: ontosage:Measurand
description: A quantity a sensor can measure, at the granularity that distinguishes one gas from another. QUDT stops at VolumeFraction, which cannot tell CO from NO2 - so these are declared here rather than borrowed.

name: ontosage:NetworkService
description: An aggregate connectivity or IT service serving spaces — wired, wireless, or a named platform. Deliberately an aggregate: per-device or per-user network monitoring would be surveillance the privacy rules forbid.

name: ontosage:Noise_Level_Sensor
description: Alias kept for graphs that label the same measurement 'noise' rather than 'sound level'.

name: ontosage:NursingRoom
description: A private nursing / baby-feeding room.

name: ontosage:OperatingRegime
description: How a building system is SUPPOSED to run: its setpoints, its occupied and unoccupied schedules, its seasonal changeover and the deviations that are approved rather than faults.

name: ontosage:Parking_Occupancy_Sensor
description: A count of parking bays that are free or occupied. Brick has no class for this: brick:Occupancy_Count_Sensor is the nearest, and it also covers entrance footfall counters and room people-counters. On the building this was developed against that one class held 257 sensors of which exactly ONE was parking, so a parking question resolved to a class it shared with 256 other things and no answer could be given — the system knew the bay count and could not reach it. Declaring the specific class is the TTL-first fix: the CLASS becomes the discriminator, so nothing downstream needs a label filter, and subclassing the Brick parent means every existing query that asks for Occupancy_Count_Sensor still finds it.

name: ontosage:ParkingArea
description: A car park or parking level. Separate from ontosage:BikeStorage (cycles) and from the accessible bays an AccessibilityFeature declares. Holding it as an Amenity lets 'where can I park' be located; how many bays are FREE is a measurement, and belongs to whatever point the building records it at, never to this record.

name: ontosage:PatrolCheckpoint
description: A point on a security circuit, with its position, the shift that walks it, when it was last verified and when it is next due. recordStatus is RECORDED rather than derived from the due time, because overdue and unverifiable are different facts with different remedies -- one needs walking, the other needs a lock or a tag fixed -- and a date alone collapses them into 'late'. expectedMinutes exists so a circuit's feasibility in a patrol window is a sum rather than a judgement.

name: ontosage:Permit
description: An authorisation to carry out controlled work (hot works, roof access, confined space, electrical isolation) for a bounded period in a bounded place. Open or closed is READ from recordStatus, never inferred from the dates: a permit past its end date that was never closed is an exception worth reporting, not a closed permit.

name: ontosage:Policy
description: A governing rule of the building — network access, fire safety, data protection, room booking — normally set out in full in an uploaded document. The triple carries the SHORT authoritative answer and, via ontosage:documentRef, names the document that holds the long form. That link is what makes document retrieval deterministic: the question is matched to the policy by lay term, then answered from the document the policy NAMES, instead of whichever chunk a similarity search happened to score highest.

name: ontosage:PotabilityStatement
description: A published statement about whether water from a given outlet or area is fit to drink, with the responsible owner and the date it was issued. A KnowledgeTopic subclass so the existing capability resolver answers it with no new code.

name: ontosage:PrayerRoom
description: A quiet multi-faith prayer or reflection space.

name: ontosage:PrinterPoint
description: A shared printing location.

name: ontosage:Procedure
description: A step-by-step process a stakeholder follows: making a complaint, booking a room, reporting lost property.

name: ontosage:PublicEvent
description: A published, visitor-facing arrangement over a space: admission times, entrance, registration policy and change history. DISTINCT FROM ontosage:Booking, which is a room held for a period — a booking can move without the published event changing, and that disagreement is precisely what a visitor asking 'has the venue changed since my invitation' needs reported.

name: ontosage:PV_Generation_Power_Sensor
description: Measures the electrical power a photovoltaic array or inverter is generating, normally in kW. Declared by OntoSage because the pinned Brick version has PV equipment (PV_Panel, PV_Array, Photovoltaic_Inverter) but no generation-power point class, so a question about solar output could only resolve to every power sensor in the building -- and was answered with the floor energy meters.

name: ontosage:QuestionIntent
description: The shape/kind of a stakeholder question (locate, quantify, trend, compare, …).

name: ontosage:Rainfall_Sensor
description: Measures precipitation depth over an interval, normally in millimetres. Declared by OntoSage because the pinned Brick version defines no precipitation class; relevant to green-roof retention and rainwater harvesting questions.

name: ontosage:Record
description: Abstract supertype for a standing record a building keeps about itself: a register row such as a fire-safety asset, a department, a workspace profile or a sustainability target. It has an owner, a status and a version rather than an interval lifecycle. Never instantiated directly.

name: ontosage:Renewable_Energy_System
description: On-site generation such as photovoltaic or solar-thermal, modelled as a system rather than a single equipment item because it spans arrays, inverters and metering.

name: ontosage:Report
description: A submitted fault/complaint/safety/feedback/suggestion record.

name: ontosage:RiskAssessment
description: A dated assessment of a hazard in a place or activity, with its review date. Overdue is computed from dueDate, exactly as ComplianceCheck does.

name: ontosage:SafetyReport
description: A health/safety concern or hazard (blocked exit, spill, trip hazard) — usually high priority.

name: ontosage:ServedZone
description: A set of spaces whose conditions are genuinely represented by a shared point — typically because one air-handling unit, one thermal zone or one distributed sensor array serves them all. Membership is a claim about the MECHANICAL design, not about geometry, and it must be validated before any answer may rest on it.

name: ontosage:Service
description: A staffed service point (reception, help desk, security desk).

name: ontosage:ServiceSchedule
description: A planned recurring operation on a space: cleaning, waste collection, planned maintenance, planned shutdown. Distinct from a WorkOrder, which is reactive: 'when is this room next cleaned' and 'who is fixing the broken tap' are different questions with different sources.

name: ontosage:ShowerFacility
description: Shower / changing facilities (e.g. for cyclists).

name: ontosage:Soil_Moisture_Sensor
description: Measures volumetric water content of a growing medium, reported as a percentage. Declared by OntoSage because the pinned Brick version defines no soil or substrate moisture class; distinct from Relative_Humidity_Sensor, which measures air.

name: ontosage:Sound_Level_Sensor
description: Measures ambient sound pressure level, normally reported in dB(A). Declared by OntoSage because the pinned Brick version defines no acoustic sensor class; the WHO indoor guideline band 30-70 dB(A) anchors its comfort scoring.

name: ontosage:SourceType
description: A category of grounding source for an answer (graph, time-series DB, floor plan, analytics, …).

name: ontosage:StakeholderGroup
description: A category of person the building serves, recorded with what they need from it, which department serves them, what they are accountable for, when they are present and how far their access reaches. DISTINCT FROM ontosage:StakeholderRole, which is a conversational persona that biases answer framing: this is operational data about a group, with an owner and effective dates, and it is a Record for that reason. No individual is modelled — a group is the finest grain this register goes to.

name: ontosage:StakeholderRole
description: A category of building stakeholder, used only to frame and prioritise answers (not for access control).

name: ontosage:StockItem
description: One stock line: a kind of item held in one store, with the quantity on hand, the level below which it is reordered, who is accountable for it and when it was last counted. FOUR KINDS ARE KEPT APART because they answer different questions: a consumable is used up, a spare is held against a named asset, loan equipment is lent and returned, and surplus is withdrawn stock available for reuse. Quantity on hand is what is on the shelf now -- anything out on loan is stated in the note and never counted as stock, and a loan line never says who has an item. STATUS FOLLOWS THE NUMBERS: a line is in stock only when quantity on hand is at or above its minimum, so a shortage is a comparison the reader can check rather than an adjective. Safety-critical stock (fire extinguishers, emergency lighting parts, first-aid supplies, hazardous chemicals) is deliberately not held here.

name: ontosage:StudyArea
description: Open study areas, collaboration pods, quiet workspaces.

name: ontosage:Suggestion
description: A proposed improvement (add a water fountain, extend café hours).

name: ontosage:SustainabilityTarget
description: A published institutional commitment against which progress is reported: a diversion rate, a carbon reduction, a consumption ceiling. Authored and cited, NEVER inferred - a target derived from the data it is meant to judge would make every trend look like success or failure by construction.

name: ontosage:Tariff
description: A registered unit rate and standing charge for a utility, valid over a period, from a named authority. Cost is computed ONLY when one of these exists. An invented unit rate produces a confident wrong number, which is the failure mode this project guards against hardest — so with no Tariff the honest answer is a decline that names the missing source.

name: ontosage:TimetabledSession
description: A scheduled teaching or institutional session in a space. Separate from Booking because the two answer different questions and have different authority: a timetable says what the institution has PLANNED, a booking says what somebody has RESERVED, and where they disagree the answer must say so rather than silently prefer one.

name: ontosage:ToiletFacility
description: Washrooms / accessible toilets.

name: ontosage:VendingMachine
description: Vending for snacks or drinks. Asked for constantly by occupants and visitors, and answerable only if the building says so — nothing in the sensor model implies it.

name: ontosage:Warranty
description: A manufacturer or installer guarantee attached to a specific asset for a period. Changes the correct answer to a maintenance question — whether the work is chargeable — which no routing fix can recover if the warranty is not modelled.

name: ontosage:Waste_Fill_Sensor
description: Reports how full a waste or recycling receptacle is, as a percentage of its capacity.

name: ontosage:Waste_Weight_Sensor
description: Reports the mass of waste in a receptacle or collected from a stream.

name: ontosage:WasteCollectionPoint
description: One bin or container: its station, what the SYSTEM records it as, what the bin is LABELLED, what its aperture physically accepts, its fill against an approved threshold, and when it is next collected. The three stream columns are separate deliberately -- a point recorded as general waste, labelled mixed recycling and fitted with a narrow slot is one people will use wrongly, and collapsing them into a single stream field makes that disagreement unrepresentable when the disagreement IS the answer. Fill threshold is per point, because a 240-litre bin in a busy atrium and a 60-litre one in a quiet corridor do not cross 'full' at the same percentage.

name: ontosage:WastePoint
description: A bin, cluster of bins or collection point where waste is deposited. An Amenity subclass so the existing capability chain locates it -- 'where are the recycling bins' needs authoring, not engineering.

name: ontosage:WasteReturn
description: One line of the waste contractor's monthly return: the weight collected from the building in one month for one stream, how it was weighed, how it was treated and what share of it was diverted from landfill. TONNES, NOT BINS: the collection point register records containers and their fill percentage, which is not a weight. A MONTH IS NOT A FIGURE UNTIL ITS RETURN IS ISSUED -- the current month is held as pending with no weight, so a question about this month has no issued answer and the honest reply is the latest complete month, dated. HOW A WEIGHT WAS OBTAINED MATTERS: a weight estimated from container volume is an estimate and must be reported as one. The building's diverted share is weighted by tonnage, never the average of the stream percentages. Weights are for the whole building: nothing here is per floor, per room or per day.

name: ontosage:WorkOrder
description: A maintenance task with an open->assigned->done lifecycle.

name: ontosage:WorkspaceProfile
description: What a space is like to WORK IN, as opposed to what it is called or how big it is. Records power, network quality, daylight, acoustic character, whether it suits a call, whether a group can use it without disturbing others, and the times it is typically busy or quiet.

name: hbco:CompositeConcept
description: A concept whose measurement requires combining multiple atomic concepts (e.g. 'thermal comfort' = temperature + humidity).

name: hbco:Concept
description: An environment/comfort concept an occupant expresses in lay language, mapped to Brick sensor classes.

name: rdf:Alt
description: The class of containers of alternatives.

name: rdf:Bag
description: The class of unordered containers.

name: rdf:CompoundLiteral
description: A class representing a compound literal.

name: rdf:HTML
description: The datatype of RDF literals storing fragments of HTML content

name: rdf:JSON
description: The datatype of RDF literals storing JSON content.

name: rdf:langString
description: The datatype of language-tagged string values

name: rdf:List
description: The class of RDF Lists.

name: rdf:PlainLiteral
description: The class of plain (i.e. untyped) literal values, as used in RIF and OWL 2

name: rdf:Property
description: The class of RDF properties.

name: rdf:Seq
description: The class of ordered containers.

name: rdf:Statement
description: The class of RDF statements.

name: rdf:XMLLiteral
description: The datatype of XML literal values.

name: rdfs:Class
description: The class of classes.

name: rdfs:Container
description: The class of RDF containers.

name: rdfs:ContainerMembershipProperty
description:
The class of container membership properties, rdf:_1, rdf:_2, ...,
                    all of which are sub-properties of 'member'.

name: rdfs:Datatype
description: The class of RDF datatypes.

name: rdfs:Literal
description: The class of literal values, eg. textual strings and integers.

name: rdfs:Resource
description: The class resource, everything.

name: owl:AllDifferent
description: The class of collections of pairwise different individuals.

name: owl:AllDisjointClasses
description: The class of collections of pairwise disjoint classes.

name: owl:AllDisjointProperties
description: The class of collections of pairwise disjoint properties.

name: owl:Annotation
description: The class of annotated annotations for which the RDF serialization consists of an annotated subject, predicate and object.

name: owl:AnnotationProperty
description: The class of annotation properties.

name: owl:AsymmetricProperty
description: The class of asymmetric properties.

name: owl:Axiom
description: The class of annotated axioms for which the RDF serialization consists of an annotated subject, predicate and object.

name: owl:Class
description: The class of OWL classes.

name: owl:DataRange
description: The class of OWL data ranges, which are special kinds of datatypes. Note: The use of the IRI owl:DataRange has been deprecated as of OWL 2. The IRI rdfs:Datatype SHOULD be used instead.

name: owl:DatatypeProperty
description: The class of data properties.

name: owl:DeprecatedClass
description: The class of deprecated classes.

name: owl:DeprecatedProperty
description: The class of deprecated properties.

name: owl:FunctionalProperty
description: The class of functional properties.

name: owl:InverseFunctionalProperty
description: The class of inverse-functional properties.

name: owl:IrreflexiveProperty
description: The class of irreflexive properties.

description: Ask whether something is abnormal or OK — 'is anything wrong?', 'any alarms?'.

description: Ask about how the space feels using lay language — resolved via Module B concepts ('is it stuffy / too warm / noisy?').

description: Compare two or more things — floors, zones, periods.

name: ontosage:Intent_Discover
description: Explore what the building has — 'what sensors are on floor 3?', 'list the equipment'.

name: ontosage:Intent_Forecast
description: Ask for a projection of a value — 'what will the temperature be tomorrow?'.

name: ontosage:Intent_Locate
description: Find where something is (amenity, room, sensor, equipment).

name: ontosage:Intent_ProcedureAsk
description: Ask how to do something — answered from a Module A ontosage:Procedure.

name: ontosage:Intent_Quantify
description: Ask for a count or a current reading — 'how many', 'what is the level right now'.

name: ontosage:Intent_Report
description: STATE a problem rather than ask a question — 'the toilet is leaking', 'the lift is broken'. Files a Module E report; distinct from asking whether something is broken.

name: ontosage:Intent_Trend
description: Ask how a value has changed over a period — 'trend', 'over the last week', 'average yesterday'.

name: ontosage:Role_Admin
description: Configures OntoSage and authors the ontology. Uses the admin console and the browsers; the only role that adds/edits triples.

name: ontosage:Role_Executive
description: A decision-maker wanting summarised, high-level answers (KPIs, headline figures) rather than raw readings.

name: ontosage:Role_FacilityManager
description: Operates the building. Asks about sensor readings, trends, anomalies, maintenance, and equipment — wants figures and evidence, not just plain answers.

name: ontosage:Role_Occupant
description: A day-to-day building user (staff, student, resident). Asks about comfort, amenities, wayfinding, and how-to procedures in plain language.

name: ontosage:Role_Researcher
description: A researcher/analyst querying the building's data and ontology. Comfortable with Brick classes, SPARQL, and raw figures.

name: ontosage:Role_SafetyOfficer
description: Responsible for health, safety, and compliance. Asks about air quality, occupancy limits, alarms, and incident reporting.

name: ontosage:Role_Student
description: A learner using the building; asks about study spaces, amenities, timetables, and how-to procedures.

name: ontosage:Role_SustainabilityOfficer
description: Focuses on energy, carbon, and efficiency. Asks about consumption, trends, and comparisons.

name: ontosage:Role_Visitor
description: A guest with no prior knowledge of the building. Asks wayfinding, amenity, and access questions.

name: ontosage:Src_CapabilityKB

name: ontosage:Src_Document
description: Prose retrieved from an uploaded manual or policy document. When the topic names its document via ontosage:documentRef the retrieval is scoped to that document; otherwise it was chosen by similarity alone and is weaker evidence.

name: ontosage:Src_FloorPlan
description: Spatial geometry answers from floor-plan manifests (areas, adjacency, block locations).

name: ontosage:Src_GraphDB
description: Structural/metadata facts answered by SPARQL over the Brick + OCBV graph.

name: ontosage:Src_Ontology
description: Amenity / knowledge-topic / policy facts asserted as triples in the building's own TTL (Module A). Authored and auditable — the answer is what the building states.

name: ontosage:Src_ReportIntake
description: The report-filing path (Module E) — used when the utterance states a problem.

name: ontosage:Src_TimeSeriesDB
description: Live sensor readings fetched by UUID from the registered time-series store.
